rippleWind.station: S111, Scotts Road (3.6 km from the bay centre)
rippleWind.method: Speed-weighted circular mean of minute wind-from bearings for a representative Singapore morning. This is a nearby land-station estimate. Only the shorter pair of ripple wave vectors follow this bearing.

processing: Copernicus Sentinel-2 L2A surface reflectance. Use the supplied scale on offset-corrected Earth Search COGs. Within the mapped bay, erode valid SCL water by two 20-m pixels and stay 55 m off the mapped shore. Fit per-date median RGB against each shortwave infrared band with Theil–Sen slopes and take the mean zero-SWIR intercept. The centre comes from pixels classified as water on at least five dates. Shore sampling and the blend radius are described in shoreCoverage. The Singapore River mouth shares the continuous water surface.

waves.ripples: The original short-wave RMS slope of 0.115 was fitted to three daytime photographs. The current morning light uses a breezier 0.1725 across the two reservoir features. This artistic choice breaks up the broad bright reflection when looking across the bay. The short-wave strength also varies across elongated wind patches. The 24 m crosswind and 82 m downwind scales and 0.36 to 1.12 gain range are visual estimates. The same gain applies to resolved ripples and their unresolved slope variance.
waves.method: Fit the metre-scale gravity-wave slope to open-water contrast in 12 windows per photograph. Compare the 1–3, 3–9 and 9–27 pixel bands after local brightness normalization. A slope of 0.04 improves all three bands in both fitted views. This represents one daylight water state over the reflectance sample area.

uncertainty: Intercepts of separate SWIR1/SWIR2 fits, averaged across the two estimates. Seasonal water and aerosol variability remain in these estimates.
daylightWater: For the morning display, use the 2026-08-22 observation. Subtract each fitted SWIR slope times its corresponding SWIR band from the same-date RGB medians, then average the two corrected estimates. This is a representative darker water state within the eight observed dates.

shoreCoverage.observation: Within the two mapped reservoir features, compare water-classified Sentinel pixels at 440–540 m to those inside 352 m. After the existing two-SWIR correction the outer median green reflectance was lower on each of the eight dates (17–26 outer pixels per date). Beyond 540 m only 3–5 pixels per date were usable and several corrected medians were negative.
shoreCoverage.blend: Keep the representative central sample through 480 m and fade to the regional water material by 600 m. The outer radius rounds the farthest stable sampled pixel to a 20 m grid cell. The existing smooth transition also applies to the gravity-wave amplitude.
